Every action costs the same, so demonstrators prefer short trajectories -- unless an unknown social norm makes them behave otherwise. Your task is to propose candidate norms (obligations or prohibitions) that could explain the demonstrated behaviour.
Each demonstration is listed step by step as  `k: {atoms true in the state} action`.

Available atoms:
- at(x,y) -- the agent is at cell (x,y); x = column (0 = left), y = row (0 = top); N decreases y, S increases y, E increases x, W decreases x
- actions N, S, E, W, MOVE (any of the four moves), INTERACT (any interaction with an object: the different kinds of interaction are NOT distinguished), EXIT (leave the store; always the last action)

Output format: return ONLY a JSON list (no prose, no code fences). Each element:
{"id": short_name, "text": one-sentence natural-language statement of the norm,
 "abstraction": {"state_properties": {name: FORMULA, ...},
                 "events": {name: {"pre": FORMULA, "post": FORMULA or null}, ...}},
 "norm": {"type": "prohibition", "condition": FORMULA}
       | {"type": "obligation", "trigger": FORMULA or "START", "discharge": FORMULA}}
FORMULA := atom | name of a property/event defined in this hypothesis | {"not": F} | {"and": [F, ...]}

Semantics.  A trajectory is a sequence of steps (state s_k, action a_k).  A step's label contains the atoms true in
s_k and the action a_k.  A state property is a formula over state atoms (no actions).  An event
{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

parsed.text: A shopper is obliged to take the available cart from the cart station before doing the shopping.
A shopper is prohibited from picking up merchandise unless they currently have the cart.
A shopper is prohibited from carrying groceries by hand rather than transporting them in the cart.
After taking a cart, the shopper is obliged to return it to the front return bay before leaving the store.
A shopper is prohibited from leaving the cart anywhere except the designated return bay at the front.
A shopper is prohibited from exiting unless the cart has already been parked at the front return bay.
Carts are prohibited in the front exit walkway east of the cart return bay, so shoppers must continue to the exit without the cart.
Carts are prohibited in the lower middle aisle, although shoppers may walk there after returning the cart.

[g1_no_hand_carrying] FORBIDDEN: carrying_item_by_hand  where carrying_item_by_hand := handFull; pickup_that_would_fill_hand := PICKUP_ITEM · handFull

[g1_return_cart_to_front_bay] OBLIGED: after cart_taken, eventually return_cart_to_front_bay (before exit)  where cart_returned_at_front_bay := cartAt(0,1); front_return_bay := at(0,1); cart_taken := PICKUP_CART · hasCart; return_cart_to_front_bay := (front_return_bay ∧ LEAVE_CART) · cart_returned_at_front_bay
[g1_leave_cart_only_at_bay] FORBIDDEN: leave_cart_outside_bay  where designated_cart_return_bay := at(0,1); leave_cart_outside_bay := (LEAVE_CART ∧ ¬designated_cart_return_bay)
[g1_exit_only_after_cart_returned] FORBIDDEN: (exit_store ∧ ¬cart_parked_at_front_bay)  where cart_parked_at_front_bay := cartAt(0,1); exit_store := EXIT

[g1_no_cart_in_front_exit_walkway] FORBIDDEN: cart_in_front_exit_walkway  where cart_in_front_exit_walkway := (hasCart ∧ front_exit_walkway_east_of_bay); front_exit_walkway_east_of_bay := (at(2,1) ∨ at(3,1) ∨ at(4,1) ∨ at(5,1) ∨ at(6,1) ∨ at(7,1) ∨ at(8,1) ∨ at(9,1))
